back: Business: how to compete in a market. Corporate: where to compete.
Value creation (what, for whom) · value configuration (how the value chain is organized) · value capture (why a margin).
Creation: guests find housing, hosts rent out · Configuration: multi-sided platform · Capture: commissions (Airbnb), payments (hosts).
A firm can create much value but capture little; capture depends on credible alternatives of customers, suppliers, partners.
Cost leadership (low cost, broad) · Differentiation (broad) · Focused cost leadership (narrow) · Focused differentiation (narrow).
Input costs (materials, labour) · economies of scale · economies of learning (experience curve).
Cost: functional, few layers, centralized staff, specialized jobs, operations main. Differentiation: flexible, marketing & product R&D main, less specialized jobs.
Costly, risky innovation · costs still matter · rivals deliver same value cheaper · WTP limited · too different (Juicero).
Unclear position between cost and differentiation + poor performance (JCPenney). Exceptions: compartmentalization, blue ocean.
WTP − costs. Cost advantage, value advantage or dual advantage.
Not capability but business model: gen-AI answers cannibalize ad-funded search and have real marginal costs.
Dig for gold (models) · sell shovels (chips, cloud) · make jewellery (complements: apps, browsers, OS).
